why: The self guard dropped, leaving only the liveness check. It happens to hold today -- this process is alive, so `isAlive(selfPid)` is true -- which is precisely what makes the mutation worth pinning: the correctness of the reaper would rest on a coincidence between two independent checks rather than on a stated rule, and any change to how liveness is determined (a permission error, a container that hides its own pid, a stubbed predicate in a test) would have it delete the worktrees of the run performing the deletion.
killedBy: staleWorkerWorktrees: collecting a killed run's leftovers (issue #664) never collects its OWN worktrees, whatever the liveness check says
